text: This report provides an update and recommendations around the next phase of procurement and construction of the George Street Revitalization project which are further described in detail in Confidential Attachment 1 and Confidential Attachment 2. In 2013, Toronto City Council approved proceeding with the George Street Revitalization project, which would include a new facility to replace the existing Seaton House men's shelter and facilitate the co-location of a long-term care home, shelters services, affordable housing, and a community service hub. City Council also approved delivering the project through an alternative financing and procurement (public-private partnership, "P3") model with Infrastructure Ontario and Lands Corporation (known as Infrastructure Ontario, "IO") acting as procurement lead.
